hero.text: Simple 40-minute lessons in three stages, each built on a unit activity in the government Pupil's Book.

blocks.heading: What a PPP lesson is
text: PPP stands for **Presentation, Practice and Production**. The teacher first presents a small piece of language in a clear situation. Pupils then practise it in controlled tasks, and finally use it for a purpose of their own. It suits large classes because each stage has a clear start and end, and it fits the activity sequence of the Sri Lankan Pupil's Books well.
Each plan below gives the book unit and activity, the learning outcome, the materials, and what happens in each stage with timings for a 40-minute period. Adapt the timings to your own timetable.

blocks.title: About these plans
text: Grade 3 is taught mainly through listening and speaking. Keep writing short and let pupils say everything before they write it. Stage times are for a 40-minute period; shorten them if your period is 30 minutes.

Every plan on this page was written by RCF English. The unit and activity names refer to the government Pupil's Book so that you can find the right page; no textbook text is reproduced here. Download it as an editable Word document or a print-ready PDF.

blocks.heading: The PPP stages in one line each
text: **Presentation:** the teacher shows the new language in a clear context. **Practice:** pupils use it in controlled tasks, usually from the Pupil's Book. **Production:** pupils use it more freely for their own purpose. **Check and close:** a quick check of learning, then homework.

blocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, I, myself and me
intro: **Book activity:** Say your name; Make your badge. **Focus:** Greeting and saying your name.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to greet a friend and say their own name using Hello! I'm ... and What's your name?
**Materials:** Paper badges, crayons, a soft ball.
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 1: Greeting and saying your name. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Wave and say Hello! I'm Teacher. Repeat with two pupils. Hold up a name badge and model: What's your name? My name is ...
Class repeats the two lines, then halves of the class say them to each other. Pass the ball: the pupil holding it answers What's your name? and asks the next pupil.
Pupils make and colour a name badge, then walk around and greet five friends using the badge.
Sing a hello song together. **Homework:** Say Hello! I'm ... to three people at home.

blocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 1, I, myself and me
intro: **Book activity:** Count, read and say; How old are you?. **Focus:** Numbers one to ten and saying your age.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to count from one to ten and say how old they are.
**Materials:** Number cards 1 to 10, the picture page with the children's ages.
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 1: Numbers one to ten and saying your age. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Count ten pencils aloud, holding up a number card for each. Model: How old are you? I'm eight.
Pupils count in pairs, taking turns (Work in pairs. Take turns). Show a number card; pupils say the number and the word.
Pupils read the speech bubbles (Hi, I'm Kumar. I'm eight years old.) and then say the same about themselves to a partner.
Count back from ten to one together. **Homework:** Count ten things at home and draw them.

blocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 1, I, myself and me
intro: **Book activity:** Listen and say; Play the game. **Focus:** Saying your grade and where you live.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say which grade they are in and where they live.
**Materials:** A ball, a simple map of the area.
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 1: Saying your grade and where you live. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Model: I'm in grade three. I live in Matara (use your own town). Ask two pupils What grade are you in? Where do you live?
Chorus and pair repetition of the two questions and answers.
Play the ball game from the book: pupils in a circle pass the ball asking Where do you live? and answering I live in ...
Three pupils introduce themselves with name, age, grade and town. **Homework:** Draw your house and write I live in ... under it.

blocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 2, Home sweet home
intro: **Book activity:** My family; Sing the song. **Focus:** Family members.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name family members and introduce them with This is my ...
**Materials:** Family picture from the book, word cards (mother, father, brother, sister).
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 2: Family members. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Point to the family picture: This is my father. This is my mother. Stick the word cards next to each person.
Pupils point and say as the teacher names each member. Teach the Family Tree song line by line.
Pupils draw their own family and introduce it to a partner: This is my sister. She is a girl.
Sing the song again with actions. **Homework:** Bring a family photo or drawing.

blocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 3, Our School
intro: **Book activity:** Read aloud; Listen and match. **Focus:** Places and people in the school.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name places in the school and match people with their jobs.
**Materials:** Picture cards: library, office room, music room, playground, herbal garden; job cards.
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 3: Places and people in the school. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Walk the class to the door and point: This is the playground. That is the library. Show the job cards: Principal, Teacher, Librarian, Security guard.
Read aloud the place names from the book. Listen and match: the teacher describes a person and pupils point to the right card.
Pairs play I'm thinking of a place: one pupil mimes (reading, dancing) and the other names the place.
Pupils name their favourite place in the school. **Homework:** Draw one place in the school and write its name.

blocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 4, My food bag
intro: **Book activity:** Talk; Look and find; Listen and make a food bag. **Focus:** Fruits and vegetables.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name common fruits and vegetables and say which ones they like.
**Materials:** Real fruits and vegetables or pictures, a paper bag.
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 4: Fruits and vegetables. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Take fruits out of a bag one by one: This is a banana. This is a carrot. Model: I like mangoes.
Look and find: pupils point to each fruit in the book picture. Sort the picture cards into fruits and vegetables.
Listen and make a food bag: the teacher says four items and pupils draw them in a paper bag shape, then tell a partner what is in their bag.
Class says which fruit most pupils like. **Homework:** Draw your favourite fruit and write I like ...

blocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 5, Animal friends
intro: **Book activity:** Look and say; Listen to the poem and recite. **Focus:** Animals and their sounds and actions.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name animals, copy their actions and recite a short poem.
**Materials:** Animal pictures or masks.
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 5: Animals and their sounds and actions. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show animal pictures and name them. Make each animal's sound and action. Model: It is a cat. It says miaow.
Look and say, then Look and find in the book picture. Listen to the poem and recite it line by line.
Pupils make a simple mask (Make a mask) and act out the animal while the class guesses.
Recite the poem with actions. **Homework:** Tell your family the name of three animals in English.

blocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 6, Clothes we wear
intro: **Book activity:** Sing this song; Look, read and match. **Focus:** Clothes and colours.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name clothes with their colours using has / I have.
**Materials:** Real clothes (a hat, a belt, a scarf), colour cards.
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 6: Clothes and colours. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Put on a hat: I have a blue hat. Point to a pupil: Nimal has a white shirt.
Sing the song (Sonia has a blue hat...) and point to the clothes. Look, read and match the clothes words with the pictures.
Pupils describe what they are wearing to a partner: I have a white shirt and a blue short.
Two pupils describe a friend while the class guesses who. **Homework:** Draw your favourite clothes and colour them.

blocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 6, Clothes we wear
intro: **Book activity:** Time; Read the time. **Focus:** Telling the time.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to read and say o'clock, quarter past, half past and quarter to.
**Materials:** A cardboard clock with moving hands.
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 6: Telling the time. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Move the clock hands: It is seven o'clock. It is half past seven. Show quarter past and quarter to.
Pupils read the times in the book. The teacher sets the clock; pupils say the time.
Pairs draw a clock face, set a time and ask What's the time?
Ask: What time do you come to school? **Homework:** Draw a clock showing the time you wake up.

blocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 7, Playing is fun
intro: **Book activity:** Listen, repeat and act; Let's play a game. **Focus:** Action words for games.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to follow and give simple action instructions such as run, jump and kick.
**Materials:** A ball, open space.
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 7: Action words for games. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Do the actions while saying them: Run! Jump! Kick the ball! Show Look! The ball rolls fast.
Listen, repeat and act: pupils copy the teacher. Simon says with the action words.
Small groups play a game while one leader gives the instructions in English.
Pupils name the game they liked best. **Homework:** Teach one action game to a brother or sister.

blocks.heading: Plan 11: Unit 8, The world around me
intro: **Book activity:** Listen, point and repeat; Listen and read. **Focus:** Things in a home garden.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name things in a garden and describe a tree using It has ...
**Materials:** A picture of a garden, a real leaf and a small branch.
blocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 8: Things in a home garden. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Point to the garden picture: This is a tree. It has leaves. It has branches. Show the real leaf and branch.
Listen, point and repeat the garden words: bush, path, tree, pond, swing, fence. Read This is my garden. It has big trees.
Pupils draw their own garden or school garden and tell a partner three things it has.
Say the Mother Nature lines together: Save water. Plant a tree. **Homework:** Water a plant at home and tell the class tomorrow.

blocks.heading: The PPP stages in one line each
text: **Presentation:** the teacher shows the new language in a clear context. **Practice:** pupils use it in controlled tasks, usually from the Pupil's Book. **Production:** pupils use it more freely for their own purpose. **Check and close:** a quick check of learning, then homework.

blocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, Hello
intro: **Book activity:** Role play; Activity 7. **Focus:** Introductions with am, is and are.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to introduce themselves and a classmate and choose am, is or are correctly.
**Materials:** The Unit 1 role play, a chart of am / is / are.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 1: Introductions with am, is and are. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Introduce yourself: I am Mrs Perera. I am your English teacher. Point to pupils: This is Nimal. He is in Grade 6. They are friends. Build the chart: I – am; he / she / it – is; we / you / they – are.
Read the role play in pairs. Chain drill: each pupil says I am ... and introduces the next pupil. Do Activity 7 (am, is or are) and check with a partner.
Groups of three write and act a short first-day meeting, using am, is and are at least five times.
Two groups perform; the class listens for am, is and are. **Homework:** Write five sentences about your family using am, is and are.

blocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 2, Leisure Lesson
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 5 and 6. **Focus:** What people are doing now (present continuous).
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to describe actions happening now with is / are + -ing.
**Materials:** The Unit 2 picture, verb cards.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 2: What people are doing now (present continuous). A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Mime writing and ask What am I doing? Write You are writing. Show the pattern am / is / are + verb-ing and spelling changes (swim – swimming, make – making).
Mime-and-guess with verb cards: She is swimming. Complete Activity 5.
Pairs describe the Unit 2 picture aloud, then write four sentences (Activity 6).
Check three -ing spellings on the board. **Homework:** Write what five family members are doing at 7 p.m. tonight.

blocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 3, Where's Everything?
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 4 and 6. **Focus:** Prepositions of place.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say and write where things are with in, on, under, near, next to and between.
**Materials:** A box, a pen, classroom objects.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 3: Prepositions of place. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Use the box and pen: The pen is in / on / under the box. Place a book between two bags and write each preposition with a sketch.
Pair work: list classroom objects and say where they are (Activity 3). Write sentences about the picture (Activity 4).
Listen and draw (Activity 6), then pupils describe their own picture for a partner to draw.
Compare drawings: which pairs matched? **Homework:** Write five sentences about your bedroom.

blocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 4, What Can You See?
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1 and 2. **Focus:** This, that, these, those.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use this / these for near things and that / those for things far away.
**Materials:** Objects placed near and far from the teacher.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 4: This, that, these, those. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Hold a pen: This is a pen. Point to one far away: That is a pen. Repeat with plurals. Draw a near / far, one / many table.
Activity 2: six sentences about things in and outside the classroom, using all four words.
Read three sentences; the class points near or far. **Homework:** Label a drawing of your table with four sentences.

blocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 5, Aunt Minoli's Kitchen
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1 and 2. **Focus:** Instructions in order.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to give instructions for a simple recipe using imperatives and first, next, then, finally.
**Materials:** Step pictures for making tea, sequence word cards.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 5: Instructions in order. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out making tea: First, boil the water. Next, put tea leaves in the pot. Point out that each instruction starts with a verb.
Match the soup steps with the pictures (Activity 1). Order the tea steps and add sequence words (Activity 2).
Groups write steps for a simple snack; one pupil reads while another mimes.
Did the mime follow the order? **Homework:** Write six steps for something you make at home.

blocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 6, What We Do
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 4, 5 and 6. **Focus:** Daily routines (present simple).
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to ask and answer about routines and report them with the -s form.
**Materials:** Find-someone-who cards.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 6: Daily routines (present simple). A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Tell your routine: I get up at 5 o'clock. Change it: She gets up at 5 o'clock. Underline the -s.
Drill Do you ...? Yes, I do. / No, I don't. Find someone who (Activity 4).
Report to the class (Activity 5) and write the findings (Activity 6).
Correct He get up → He gets up. **Homework:** Write about a family member's day in six sentences.

blocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 7, A Fine Day
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 4 and 5. **Focus:** Weather words and on / in / at.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name the weather and use on for days, in for months and at for times.
**Materials:** A calendar, weather symbol cards.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 7: Weather words and on / in / at. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show the calendar: My birthday is in June, on the 12th, at 4 o'clock. Build the rule table.
Listen and name the weather symbols (Activity 3). Complete the on / in / at sentences.
Pairs interview each other about birthdays and times and write three true sentences.
Quick-fire: time word → preposition. **Homework:** Keep a weather diary for three days.

blocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 8, A Visit to the Zoo
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 5, 6 and 7. **Focus:** Ability with can and can't.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say what people and animals can and cannot do.
**Materials:** Animal pictures, an ability chart.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 8: Ability with can and can't. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: A fish can swim. A fish can't climb. Show that can never takes -s.
Match sentences and pictures (Activity 5). Complete the chart in pairs (Activity 6).
Tell the class about yourself and a friend (Activity 7): I can swim, but my friend can't.
Vote on the most surprising ability. **Homework:** Write six sentences about what you can and can't do.

blocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 9, Sugar or Sand
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 5, 6 and 7. **Focus:** Pronouns.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to replace repeated nouns with the correct pronoun.
**Materials:** A short repetitive text on the board, the Unit 9 story.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 9: Pronouns. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read: Amal has a bag. Amal's bag is red. Ask what sounds strange. Rewrite with pronouns and list them.
Circle the pronouns (Activity 5). Match and replace (Activities 6 and 7).
Pairs rewrite a paragraph that repeats a name, using pronouns.
Two pairs read aloud. **Homework:** Write about a friend using five pronouns.

blocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 10, Was It Yesterday?
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 2, 4 and 5. **Focus:** The simple past.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say what they did yesterday with regular and irregular past forms.
**Materials:** A regular / irregular verb table.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 10: The simple past. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Tell a story: Yesterday I visited my grandmother. I went by bus. Sort the verbs into +ed and irregular.
Find the past forms in the role play (Activity 2). Complete the diary flow chart (Activity 4).
Each pupil says one thing they did yesterday (Activity 5) and writes three more.
Add new verbs to the class table. **Homework:** Write a six-sentence diary entry about last weekend.

blocks.heading: Plan 11: Unit 11, Eco Friends
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1 and 2. **Focus:** Free-time activities.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to write a short paragraph about their free time with reasons.
**Materials:** The Unit 11 role play, a paragraph frame.
blocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 11: Free-time activities. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the role play and list what the friends like to do. Model: In my free time, I like to read because ...
Build a word bank. Pairs talk about what they like and why.
Write a five- or six-sentence paragraph (Activity 2) using like to / enjoy and because.
Swap: one thing done well, one to improve. **Homework:** Add a picture and bring it to display.

blocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, What You See
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 4 and 5. **Focus:** Opposites and synonyms.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to give the opposite of common adjectives and pick out words with similar meanings.
**Materials:** Picture pairs (big / small, hot / cold), word cards.
blocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 1: Opposites and synonyms. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show picture pairs and elicit the opposites. Explain synonyms with warm – hot and happy – glad.
Write opposites under the pictures (Activity 3) and match opposites (Activity 4). Circle the two synonyms in each set (Activity 5).
Pairs describe a classmate's bag with three adjectives; the partner replies with the opposites or a synonym.
Opposites race: teams of two, teacher calls a word. **Homework:** Write ten opposite pairs of your own.

blocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 2, Friends Indeed
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1, 2 and 3. **Focus:** Reading a story and writing instructions.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to answer questions on Fifi's story and write clear instructions in order.
**Materials:** Fifi's story, instruction strips cut up for ordering.
blocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 2: Reading a story and writing instructions. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Pre-teach glass, spacious and freely, then read Fifi's story aloud. Show how instructions begin with a verb and use then, next.
Answer the Activity 1 questions in pairs. Put the cut-up instructions in order (Activity 2).
Groups design a simple anti-dengue poster and write four instructions to go with it (Activity 3).
Groups show their posters. **Homework:** Write five instructions for looking after a pet.

blocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 3, Pleasure
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1, 5 and 7. **Focus:** Was, were and will be.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use was / were for the past and will be for the future when telling a story.
**Materials:** The Perahera dialogue, the Merryland story.
blocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 3: Was, were and will be. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out the Perahera dialogue with two pupils. Draw a timeline: yesterday – was / were, tomorrow – will be.
Fill in the Merryland story with was, were or will be (Activity 5). Listen and match letters to the playground passage (Activity 7).
Pairs tell each other about a festival they saw and one they will see.
Three pupils report their partner's answers. **Homework:** Write six sentences about a festival, past and future.

blocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 4, A Busy Day
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1, 3 and 9. **Focus:** Reading a notice and possessive pronouns.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to find information in a notice and use mine, yours, his, hers, ours and theirs.
**Materials:** The scout notice, pupils' own pens and books.
blocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 4: Reading a notice and possessive pronouns. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out Lahiru's busy day. Pick up a pupil's pen: Is this yours? Yes, it's mine. Build the list.
Complete the table from the notice (Activity 3). Fill in the possessive pronouns (Activity 9).
Lost-property game: the teacher collects objects and pupils claim them using the pronouns.
Correct: This book is her's → hers. **Homework:** Write a notice for a class event.

blocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 5, Once Upon a Time
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 4 and 8. **Focus:** Joining sentences with and, but, or and when.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to combine short sentences using and, but, or and when.
**Materials:** Sentence strips about early people.
blocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 5: Joining sentences with and, but, or and when. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show two strips: Early people lived in caves. They hunted animals. Join them with and. Contrast and, but, or and when with examples.
Combine the sentences (Activity 3). Join sentences with when (Activity 8).
Groups speak about the journey of human civilisation, each pupil giving one joined sentence (Activity 4).
Note the best joined sentences on the board. **Homework:** Write a short paragraph about a museum visit using when twice.

blocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 6, Better Safe Than Sorry
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1, 3 and 4. **Focus:** Must, should, would and can.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to give advice and rules with must and should and write a short note.
**Materials:** The Suganya dialogue, a get-well card.
blocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 6: Must, should, would and can. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out Suganya is Absent Today. Write rules and advice: You must wash your hands. You should rest.
Complete the sentences with must, should, would or can (Activity 3).
Pupils write Suganya's thank-you note to her friends (Activity 4).
Read two notes aloud. **Homework:** Make a get-well card for someone you know.

blocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 7, Around the Country
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1, 6 and 8. **Focus:** Adverbs and speaking about places.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use adverbs to describe how things happen and speak for one minute about a place.
**Materials:** Ruvini's speech, A Trip to Jaffna, adverb cards.
blocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 7: Adverbs and speaking about places. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read Ruvini's speech. Pupils answer the Activity 1 questions. Show adverbs: The train went slowly. They arrived safely.
Pupils choose a place and speak about it for a minute (Activity 8).
Class gives one compliment to each speaker. **Homework:** Write a description of a place you visited.

blocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 8, Wonders Around Us
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 2, 3 and 6. **Focus:** Reading for information and daily schedules.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to take notes in a table from descriptions and talk about their daily schedule.
**Materials:** Pictures of famous monuments, a blank table.
blocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 8: Reading for information and daily schedules. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show the monuments and ask what pupils know. Model a schedule: 6.30 a.m. – I have breakfast.
Match descriptions and pictures (Activity 2) and complete the table (Activity 3).
Pupils write their own schedule and compare it with a partner (Activity 6).
Pairs report one difference. **Homework:** Find one fact about a Sri Lankan monument.

blocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 9, Our Beautiful World
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 4, 5 and 6. **Focus:** Prepositions of movement.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use up, down, over, into, below and next to to describe a picture.
**Materials:** The Unit 9 picture, a toy car or ball.
blocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 9: Prepositions of movement. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Move a toy: It goes up the hill. It goes over the bridge. Write the prepositions with arrows.
Complete the sentences about the pictures (Activity 4).
Describe the picture with the given words (Activity 5), then do the describe-and-draw task (Activity 6).
Compare drawings with the originals. **Homework:** Write five sentences about your way to school.

blocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 10, Future
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 2, 3 and 7. **Focus:** Predictions with will and won't.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to make and discuss predictions about life in the future.
**Materials:** The BBC predictions text.
blocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 10: Predictions with will and won't. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read two predictions and ask Will this come true? Show will / won't + verb.
Make sentences with will / won't (Activity 7). Discuss the predictions (Activity 2).
Groups write and present a prediction for one category (Activity 3).
Class votes on the most likely prediction. **Homework:** Write five predictions about your village in 2050.

blocks.title: About these plans
text: The Grade 8 book numbers its activities by unit (1.1, 1.2 and so on). Stage times are for a 40-minute period.

Every plan on this page was written by RCF English. The unit and activity names refer to the government Pupil's Book so that you can find the right page; no textbook text is reproduced here. Download it as an editable Word document or a print-ready PDF.

blocks.heading: The PPP stages in one line each
text: **Presentation:** the teacher shows the new language in a clear context. **Practice:** pupils use it in controlled tasks, usually from the Pupil's Book. **Production:** pupils use it more freely for their own purpose. **Check and close:** a quick check of learning, then homework.

blocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, Plan the Work, Work the Plan
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3. **Focus:** Reflexive pronouns.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use myself, yourself, himself and so on correctly in sentences.
**Materials:** The English Day planning dialogue.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 1: Reflexive pronouns. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out 1.1. Pick out We did it ourselves. List the reflexive pronouns beside the subject pronouns.
Answer the 1.2 questions. Rearrange the words into sentences (1.3).
Pairs describe something they did by themselves last week.
Correct hisself → himself. **Homework:** Write five sentences about things you do yourself.

blocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 1, Plan the Work, Work the Plan
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1.7 and 1.9. **Focus:** Plural nouns and a friendly letter.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to form regular and irregular plurals and plan a friendly letter.
**Materials:** Amitha's letter.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 1: Plural nouns and a friendly letter. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Write a cup, a boot, a knife, a child and elicit the plurals. Read Amitha's letter aloud; label its parts.
Pupils write a short letter to a pen friend about a trip they are planning.
Check the address and greeting layout. **Homework:** Finish the letter neatly.

blocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 2, Winged Friends
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 2.5, 2.6 and 2.7. **Focus:** Must, have to and should.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to express rules, needs and advice with must, have to / has to and should.
**Materials:** The substitution table in 2.5.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 2: Must, have to and should. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Contrast: You must wear a seat belt (rule). You should rest (advice). Add have to / has to.
Build sentences from the table (2.5). Complete the blanks (2.6).
Write three sentences each with the three forms and their negatives (2.7).
Pairs read and correct each other. **Homework:** Write rules for looking after birds.

blocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 3, Let's Be Considerate
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3.1 and 3.3. **Focus:** Joining sentences with since and as.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to join a reason and a result using since and as.
**Materials:** The bus-stop role play.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 3: Joining sentences with since and as. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out 3.1. Show: Since it was raining, we stayed home.
Pupils write three sentences about kind acts using since and as.
Share the kindest act. **Homework:** Write a short paragraph on courtesy.

blocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 3, Let's Be Considerate
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3.5 and 3.8. **Focus:** Reading a story aloud and tongue twisters.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to read aloud clearly with good pace and pronunciation.
**Materials:** The Magic Words story, tongue twisters.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 3: Reading a story aloud and tongue twisters. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Model-read part of The Magic Words. Say the tongue twisters slowly, then faster.
Pairs read the story, taking turns by paragraph.
Groups perform the story as a short drama with the magic words.
Tongue twister challenge. **Homework:** Practise one tongue twister at home.

blocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 4, Mother Nature
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 4.5, 4.6 and 4.7. **Focus:** Prepositions and instructions.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use prepositions in instructions and label a picture from a description.
**Materials:** The picture for 4.7.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 4: Prepositions and instructions. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Review prepositions with classroom objects. Read the 4.6 instructions aloud.
Put the instructions in the correct order (4.6).
Listen and label the picture (4.7), then pairs describe their own picture.
Check labels together. **Homework:** Write instructions for planting a tree.

blocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 5, Between the Miles
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 5.2 and 5.6. **Focus:** Word building and comparisons.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to add -ly, -ful, -ness and -less to base words and use comparatives and superlatives.
**Materials:** The word-building table.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 5: Word building and comparisons. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show care → careful, careless, carefully. Compare three pupils' heights: taller, the tallest.
Complete the table (5.2) and the worksheet (5.6).
Pupils describe one of the smallest things they know (5.5).
Share one comparison. **Homework:** Write six comparison sentences about your family.

blocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 6, When We Are Together
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 6.5, 6.6 and 6.7. **Focus:** The passive voice (present).
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to recognise and form present simple passive sentences.
**Materials:** The roti-making pictures.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 6: The passive voice (present). A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show English is spoken all over the world. Ask who speaks it. Build be + past participle.
Match the roti pictures with the steps (6.5). Fill in the verb forms (6.6).
Find the passive sentences in A Day in the Life of a News Reader (6.7) and describe how tea is made in the passive.
Read two passive sentences aloud. **Homework:** Describe how a local food is made.

blocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 7, The World of Children
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 7.3, 7.8 and 7.9. **Focus:** Past passive and a letter.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to rewrite past events in the passive and write a descriptive letter.
**Materials:** Sigiriya information table.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 7: Past passive and a letter. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show: Sigiriya was built by King Kashyapa. Review letter layout.
Rewrite the historical events in the passive (7.3).
Order the Sigiriya information (7.8) and write Sahan's letter (7.9).
Peer-check the layout. **Homework:** Write about a place you visited.

blocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 8, It's a Small World
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 8.4, 8.5 and 8.7. **Focus:** Future passive and writing an article.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use will be + past participle and write a short news article.
**Materials:** Newspaper cuttings.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 8: Future passive and writing an article. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show: The match will be played tomorrow. Point out the parts of a newspaper article.
Write a short article in steps (8.7) about a school event.
Read two headlines aloud. **Homework:** Collect one English news headline.

blocks.heading: Plan 11: Unit 9, On Top of the World
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 9.2 to 9.5. **Focus:** Adverbs of frequency.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely and never.
**Materials:** A frequency scale from 0% to 100%.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 9: Adverbs of frequency. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Place the adverbs on the scale. I always brush my teeth. I never ...
Fill in the conversation (9.2) and write sentences from the pictures (9.3).
Group sentence chain (9.4), then write a paragraph (9.5).
Check adverb position. **Homework:** Write about your weekend habits.

blocks.heading: Plan 12: Unit 10, Beyond the Classroom
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 10.3 and 10.6. **Focus:** The past perfect and telling stories.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use the past perfect to show which past action happened first.
**Materials:** The English Day conversation, a timeline.
blocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 10: The past perfect and telling stories. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show: When I arrived, the bus had left. Draw two past points on a timeline.
Groups tell interesting stories and write one using inverted commas (10.6).
One group reads its story. **Homework:** Write a story ending with a surprise.

blocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, Everybody Is Good at Something
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 4 and 7. **Focus:** Collective nouns and subject–verb agreement.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to choose is / are and has / have with collective nouns and write a paragraph about a friend.
**Materials:** The TV programme dialogue.
blocks.caption: Grade 9, Unit 1: Collective nouns and subject–verb agreement. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out Activity 1. Show: The team is ready. The crew has arrived.
Write a paragraph about a best friend's talent for the wall newspaper (Activity 7).
Read two paragraphs aloud. **Homework:** Write about your own talent.

blocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 2, May I Help You?
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1, 5 and 8. **Focus:** Shopping language and commas in lists.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use shopping expressions and punctuate lists correctly.
**Materials:** A grocery list, price cards.
blocks.caption: Grade 9, Unit 2: Shopping language and commas in lists. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out the supermarket dialogue. Show: We need rice, sugar and dhal. Point to the commas.
Insert commas (Activity 8) and read the sentences aloud, pausing at commas.
Groups prepare a grocery list and role-play shopping (Activity 5).
One group performs. **Homework:** Write a shopping list and a short dialogue.

blocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 3, Meeting
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 7 and 8. **Focus:** Greetings and adjectives.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use greetings for different occasions and describe with adjectives.
**Materials:** Greeting pictures.
blocks.caption: Grade 9, Unit 3: Greetings and adjectives. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show the pictures and elicit the greetings. Find the adjectives in Activity 6.
Write the greetings (Activity 3). Write sentences with the adjectives (Activity 7).
Groups plan points for a speech on healthy food (Activity 8).
One group presents. **Homework:** Write the speech in full.

blocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 4, Extinct Friends
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 4 and 8. **Focus:** Retelling a story.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to retell a story in their own words and speak about an extinct animal.
**Materials:** The Ice Age story, dinosaur pictures.
blocks.caption: Grade 9, Unit 4: Retelling a story. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out Nethula's Tour to the Ice Age. Model a retelling with first, then, finally.
Pupils relate the dream to a partner (Activity 3).
Write the story in own words (Activity 4) and speak about an extinct creature (Activity 8).
Pairs swap and check sequence words. **Homework:** Find three facts about an extinct animal.

blocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 5, A Second Chance Called Tomorrow
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 5, 10 and 12. **Focus:** The passive and a congratulation letter.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to transform active sentences into the passive and write a congratulatory letter.
**Materials:** The 100 Metres extract.
blocks.caption: Grade 9, Unit 5: The passive and a congratulation letter. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the extract and discuss Mudalihamy's victory. Show: Rahim wrote a letter → A letter was written by Rahim.
Check the letter format. **Homework:** Write five passive sentences about your school.

blocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 6, Art
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 2, 3 and 5. **Focus:** Pronunciation and using a dictionary.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use dictionary entries to find meanings and word classes.
**Materials:** Dictionaries, the dictionary page.
blocks.caption: Grade 9, Unit 6: Pronunciation and using a dictionary. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Say the words in Activity 2 and find the shared sound. Explain a dictionary entry: headword, word class, meaning.
Use the highlighted words in the text in new sentences (Activity 5).
Dictionary race. **Homework:** Find five new words and their meanings.

blocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 7, Where We Are
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 4 and 6. **Focus:** Speaking on a topic and the passive.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to give a short talk and change sentences into the passive, leaving out the doer when not needed.
**Materials:** Pictures of dwellings.
blocks.caption: Grade 9, Unit 7: Speaking on a topic and the passive. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show the dwellings and name them. Model a one-minute talk on Earth is Our Home.
Pupils give their own talk (Activity 3) and begin a picture dictionary of dwellings (Activity 4).
Peer feedback on eye contact and clarity. **Homework:** Complete the picture dictionary.

blocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 8, Success Through Creativity
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 5 and 8. **Focus:** Relative pronouns and writing instructions.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to join ideas with who, which, whose, where and when and write upcycling instructions.
**Materials:** An empty bottle or tin.
blocks.caption: Grade 9, Unit 8: Relative pronouns and writing instructions. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read Upcycling – Turning Trash into Treasure. Show: This is the bottle which I turned into a vase.
Write instructions for upcycling an object (Activity 8).
Groups show their ideas. **Homework:** Make the upcycled object.

blocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 9, The Greatest Wealth
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 5, 6 and 7. **Focus:** Conditional sentences.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to build first and second conditional sentences.
**Materials:** The conditional table.
blocks.caption: Grade 9, Unit 9: Conditional sentences. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show: If we exercise, we will be healthy. If I had time, I would ... Contrast real and imagined situations.
Build sentences from the table (Activity 5) and match clauses (Activity 7).
Complete the clauses with own ideas (Activity 6).
Share the most creative sentence. **Homework:** Write five sentences about good health.

blocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 10, Be Happy, Be Bright, Be You!
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1 to 3. **Focus:** Reported speech.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to report statements and questions.
**Materials:** The subject-choice dialogue.
blocks.caption: Grade 9, Unit 10: Reported speech. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out Activity 1. Show how Raju reported the conversation.
Pairs interview each other about subject choices and report the answers.
Check tense changes. **Homework:** Report a conversation from home.

text: One plan for each of the fourteen units. Stage times are for a 40-minute period. Link the writing tasks to the O/L paper formats as you go.

blocks.heading: The PPP stages in one line each
text: **Presentation:** the teacher shows the new language in a clear context. **Practice:** pupils use it in controlled tasks, usually from the Pupil's Book. **Production:** pupils use it more freely for their own purpose. **Check and close:** a quick check of learning, then homework.

blocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, People
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 2, 3 and 4. **Focus:** Describing appearance.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to describe a person's appearance using adjectives in the right order.
**Materials:** Pictures of people.
blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 1: Describing appearance. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Describe a picture: She has long, black hair. Build a word bank by category.
Describe the pictures (Activity 2) and identify the people (Activity 3).
Write a description of the class teacher and present it (Activity 4).
Class guesses who is being described. **Homework:** Describe a family member.

blocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 2, On Your Way
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1, 2 and 4. **Focus:** Giving directions.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to read a map and give directions.
**Materials:** The map, a school plan.
blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 2: Giving directions. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Model directions on the map: Go straight, turn left. List direction phrases.
Mark the way on the map (Activity 1) and identify places (Activity 2).
Draw a school map and describe it (Activity 4).
Pairs test each other's directions. **Homework:** Write directions from school to your home.

blocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 3, Travel
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 5 and 6. **Focus:** Present continuous passive.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to describe what is being done with is / are being + past participle.
**Materials:** Pictures of the hotel crew at work.
blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 3: Present continuous passive. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show: The goods are being loaded. Build the form on the board.
Form passive sentences for the picture (Activity 6).
Peer-check the verb forms. **Homework:** Describe your school at 8 a.m.

blocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 4, Let's Talk
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1, 4 and 7. **Focus:** Asking questions and interviewing.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to form different question types and interview a partner.
**Materials:** Find-someone-who sheet.
blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 4: Asking questions and interviewing. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Model the question types: yes/no, wh-, tag questions. Read the telephone conversation aloud.
Interview a friend about future plans (Activity 4).
Report findings. **Homework:** Write interview questions for a local hero.

blocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 5, Best Practices
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 4 and 5. **Focus:** Writing a formal letter.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to plan and write a formal letter of complaint.
**Materials:** The letter of complaint.
blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 5: Writing a formal letter. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the letter-writing instructions (Activity 4). Label the parts of the letter.
Write a letter of complaint about a local problem.
Peer-check with a checklist. **Homework:** Finish and correct the letter.

blocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 6, Information
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 4, 5 and 6. **Focus:** Writing a paragraph from a grid.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use information in a grid to write a paragraph about a book.
**Materials:** The book grid.
blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 6: Writing a paragraph from a grid. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the newspapers paragraph. Show how the grid becomes sentences.
Write a paragraph from Hiruni's grid (Activity 5).
Complete a grid about a book you read and write a paragraph (Activity 6).
Share one paragraph. **Homework:** Write about your favourite book.

blocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 7, Learning Is Fun
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 2 and 3. **Focus:** Describing a bar chart.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to describe survey results from a bar chart.
**Materials:** The bar chart.
blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 7: Describing a bar chart. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Model: Most students prefer ... List comparison phrases.
Conduct a class survey and describe the result (Activity 3).
Present one result. **Homework:** Write a report on the class survey.

blocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 8, Healthy Food
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 8 and 9. **Focus:** Connectives of contrast.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to join ideas with although, even though and in spite of.
**Materials:** The finger millet passage.
blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 8: Connectives of contrast. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show: Although it is cheap, it is nutritious. Contrast although and in spite of.
Join sentence pairs (Activity 9) and write about homemade food.

blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 9: Reading a brochure and planning a poster. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the brochure. Point out features of a good poster.
Plan a poster for a nature exhibition (Activity 7).
Display the posters. **Homework:** Complete the poster.

blocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 10, Personality
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 2 and 7. **Focus:** Ought to and need; interviewing.

blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 10: Ought to and need; interviewing. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 11: Job advertisements and applications. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

blocks.caption: Grade 10, Unit 12: Reported speech and completing an essay. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

blocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, Our Responsibilities
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 7, 8 and 10. **Focus:** Modals for advice.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to give advice about responsible citizenship using modals.
**Materials:** The vandalism article.
blocks.caption: Grade 11, Unit 1: Modals for advice. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

Write instructions (Activity 7) and sentences from the picture (Activity 8).

blocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 2, Facing Challenges
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 5, 7 and 8. **Focus:** Organising an event and a speech.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to plan a morning assembly and organise a speech with a mind map.
**Materials:** The assembly discussion, a mind map.
blocks.caption: Grade 11, Unit 2: Organising an event and a speech. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out the assembly discussion (Activity 5). Show Kamalesh's mind map.
Number the events from the announcements (Activity 7).
Prepare a mind map and speech in groups (Activity 8).
One group delivers the speech. **Homework:** Write the speech in full.

blocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 3, Great Lanka
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 6, 7 and 8. **Focus:** Adjectives and a presentation on Sri Lanka.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use adjectives and past forms to present information about Sri Lanka.
**Materials:** A map of Sri Lanka.
blocks.caption: Grade 11, Unit 3: Adjectives and a presentation on Sri Lanka. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the documentary conversation. Find the adjectives (Activity 6).
Peer feedback. **Homework:** Write a description of a place in Sri Lanka.

blocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 4, For a Better Tomorrow
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 4, 5 and 6. **Focus:** Paragraph from a tree diagram and reported speech.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to write a paragraph from a diagram and report an interview.
**Materials:** The three R's tree diagram.
blocks.caption: Grade 11, Unit 4: Paragraph from a tree diagram and reported speech. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Practise the TV interview (Activity 1). Show how the diagram becomes a paragraph.
Write about the three R's (Activity 4). Convert sentences to reported speech (Activity 6).
Write and act an interview script (Activity 5).

blocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 5, Best Use of Time
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 7 and 8. **Focus:** Apologies and advertisements.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to write an apology and understand a newspaper advertisement.
**Materials:** The newspaper advertisement.
blocks.caption: Grade 11, Unit 5: Apologies and advertisements. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Act out the Rajan and Samith dialogue. Show apology phrases.
List the advantages of working on time (Activity 3).
Write an apology to the master-in-charge (Activity 7) and study the advertisement (Activity 8).
Read an apology aloud. **Homework:** Write a timetable for your study week.

blocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 6, A Moment of Fun
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 4 and 8. **Focus:** Determiners and writing a notice.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use determiners and write a notice.
**Materials:** The drama notice.
blocks.caption: Grade 11, Unit 6: Determiners and writing a notice. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

Prepare a notice for an event (Activity 8).
Check the notice format. **Homework:** Write a notice for a school club.

blocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 7, A Simple Living
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 1, 5 and 7. **Focus:** Instructions and collective nouns.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to write instructions and use collective nouns.
**Materials:** Instruction pictures.
blocks.caption: Grade 11, Unit 7: Instructions and collective nouns. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show the pictures and model instructions. Show: a bunch of grapes, a flock of birds.
Write instructions for the pictures (Activity 1). Form collective nouns (Activity 5).
Complete the collective noun grid (Activities 6 and 7) and use them in a paragraph.
Collective noun quiz. **Homework:** Write about a simple life.

blocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 8, Reading Is Fun
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 7 and 8. **Focus:** Adjectives and a letter of inquiry.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use adjectives and write a formal letter of inquiry.
**Materials:** The Robinson Crusoe extract.
blocks.caption: Grade 11, Unit 8: Adjectives and a letter of inquiry. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Discuss buying books for the Readers' Club (Activity 7).
Write a letter to a bookshop manager (Activity 8).
Check the letter format. **Homework:** Finish the letter.

blocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 9, Enigma
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 4, 5 and 7. **Focus:** Writing from a data sheet and debating.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to write a report from notes and take part in a debate.
**Materials:** The data sheet.
blocks.caption: Grade 11, Unit 9: Writing from a data sheet and debating. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the telephone dialogue (Activity 1). Model turning notes into sentences.
Complete the data sheet (Activity 4) and write the incident (Activity 5).
Hold a debate on a given topic (Activity 7).
Class decides the winning side. **Homework:** Write a description of a mystery.

blocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 10, Choices in Life
intro: **Book activity:** Activities 3, 6 and 7. **Focus:** Goal setting and an essay.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to set personal goals and write an essay about ambitions.
**Materials:** The goal-setting flow chart.
blocks.caption: Grade 11, Unit 10: Goal setting and an essay. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read Setting Your Personal Goals. Complete the flow chart (Activity 3).
Talk to a partner about goals (Activity 6).
Write an essay about goals and ambitions (Activity 7).

blocks.title: About these plans
text: Grades 12 and 13 share one General English textbook with eight units, so there is no separate Grade 12 or Grade 13 book. These twenty plans (ten for each year) follow the eight units in order. Your school's scheme decides which units fall in Grade 12 and which in Grade 13. Stage times are for a 40-minute period.

Every plan on this page was written by RCF English. The unit and activity names refer to the government Pupil's Book so that you can find the right page; no textbook text is reproduced here. Download it as an editable Word document or a print-ready PDF.

blocks.heading: The PPP stages in one line each
text: **Presentation:** the teacher shows the new language in a clear context. **Practice:** students use it in controlled tasks, usually from the Pupil's Book. **Production:** students use it more freely for their own purpose. **Check and close:** a quick check of learning, then homework.

blocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, Sri Lankan Achievers
intro: **Book activity:** Reading 1 (an everyday hero). **Focus:** Reading for gist and detail.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to identify the main idea of a story and explain why a person is admired.
**Materials:** The Reading 1 text.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 1: Reading for gist and detail. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Pairwork from the book: think of someone you admire and give two reasons. Pre-teach key words from the story.
Read for gist, then answer the detail questions.
Groups write a short profile of an everyday hero from their own village.
Share one profile. **Homework:** Write a 150-word paragraph about someone you admire.

blocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 1, Sri Lankan Achievers
intro: **Book activity:** Listening 1; Writing. **Focus:** Listening for specific information.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to note key facts from a talk and write a short profile of an achiever.
**Materials:** The listening text (download from edupub.gov.lk), the achievers table.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 1: Listening for specific information. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Discuss the famous Sri Lankans in Before Listening. Show how to take notes in a table.
Complete the achievements table (Writing) and write a short profile of one achiever.
Peer-check facts. **Homework:** Research another Sri Lankan achiever.

blocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 2, Living in Harmony
intro: **Book activity:** Speaking and Writing. **Focus:** Describing a picture and people.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to describe a picture and a friend using appropriate adjectives.
**Materials:** The Unit 2 picture.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 2: Describing a picture and people. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Describe the picture with the class: what are the children feeling? Show useful phrases: S/he likes ... S/he thinks ...
Write a short description of a friend using the sentence guide.
Read two descriptions. **Homework:** Write about harmony in your school.

blocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 2, Living in Harmony
intro: **Book activity:** Grammar: conditionals and modal verbs. **Focus:** Conditionals and modals.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to use conditional sentences and modal verbs to talk about coexistence.
**Materials:** The harmony quotation.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 2: Conditionals and modals. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the quotation: If there is righteousness in the heart ... Show the first and second conditional forms.
Groups write five rules for living in harmony using modals.
Share the rules. **Homework:** Write a paragraph using three conditionals.

blocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 3, Relationships
intro: **Book activity:** Speaking: quotations. **Focus:** Discussing meaning.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to discuss the meaning of quotations and give reasons.
**Materials:** The quotations.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 3: Discussing meaning. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the quotations. Show discussion phrases: I think it means ...
Class votes on the best interpretation. **Homework:** Write a quotation of your own and explain it.

blocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 3, Relationships
intro: **Book activity:** Writing: a story. **Focus:** Process writing.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a story through prewriting, drafting, feedback and revising.
**Materials:** The process-writing steps.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 3: Process writing. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Explain the steps in the book. Model prewriting with a mind map.
Share one story. **Homework:** Finish the final draft.

blocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 3, Relationships
intro: **Book activity:** Speaking: mini debates; Writing: essay. **Focus:** Debating and a discursive essay.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to take part in a mini debate and write a 250-word essay discussing both sides.
**Materials:** The debate topics.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 3: Debating and a discursive essay. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Explain proposition and opposition. Show essay structure: introduction, both sides, conclusion.
Write a 250-word essay on one topic.

blocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 4, English as a Local and Global Language
intro: **Book activity:** Speaking and Writing 1. **Focus:** Discussing advantages and difficulties.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to list and explain the advantages and difficulties of learning English.
**Materials:** The discussion questions.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 4: Discussing advantages and difficulties. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Discuss the two questions. Show how to support a point with an example.
Groups make a common list and select the six best points.
Share one paragraph. **Homework:** Write about your own English learning.

blocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 4, English as a Local and Global Language
intro: **Book activity:** Speaking 3; Language focus. **Focus:** Describing feelings and hopes.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to describe a picture and express feelings and hopes.
**Materials:** The rural English class picture.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 4: Describing feelings and hopes. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Describe the picture. Show phrases: I hope ... I wish ...
Pairwork: imagine being a student in the picture.
Write a short paragraph about hopes for learning English.
Read one paragraph. **Homework:** Write about your ideal English class.

blocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 4, English as a Local and Global Language
intro: **Book activity:** Grammar: future tenses. **Focus:** Future forms.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to use will, going to and the present continuous for the future.
**Materials:** Future forms table.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 4: Future forms. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show the three future forms. Contrast plans and predictions.
Pairs talk about their plans after A/L.
Share one plan. **Homework:** Write about your plans.

blocks.heading: Plan 11: Unit 5, Crime and Social Responsibility
intro: **Book activity:** Speaking 1; Reading 1. **Focus:** Vocabulary of crime.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to understand crime vocabulary and summarise news items.
**Materials:** The dictionary definitions, the news items.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 5: Vocabulary of crime. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Discuss the definitions of crime. Pre-teach vocabulary.
Read the six news items and answer the questions.
Summarise one news item for the class.
Share summaries. **Homework:** Find a news item and summarise it.

blocks.heading: Plan 12: Unit 5, Crime and Social Responsibility
intro: **Book activity:** Reading 2. **Focus:** Guessing meaning from context.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to guess the meaning of words from context.
**Materials:** Laws in different countries.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 5: Guessing meaning from context. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show strategies for guessing meaning. Read the first description together.
Read and guess the bold words.
Discuss which law is most surprising and why.
Share views. **Homework:** Write about a law you would change.

blocks.heading: Plan 13: Unit 5, Crime and Social Responsibility
intro: **Book activity:** Grammar: direct and reported speech. **Focus:** Reported speech.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to change direct speech into reported speech.
**Materials:** The monastery passage.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 5: Reported speech. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the passage. Show the tense and pronoun changes.
Report a conversation from the passage.
Check tense changes. **Homework:** Report a conversation from home.

blocks.heading: Plan 14: Unit 6, The Cyber World
intro: **Book activity:** Reading 1; Writing emails. **Focus:** Formal emails.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a formal email with the correct structure and tone.
**Materials:** The model emails.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 6: Formal emails. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Discuss ways of keeping in touch. Show the structure of a formal email.
Write a formal email to a principal about a prefects' day (Writing task).

blocks.heading: Plan 15: Unit 6, The Cyber World
intro: **Book activity:** Speaking: making a presentation. **Focus:** Presentation skills.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to plan and deliver a short presentation.
**Materials:** The presentation guide.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 6: Presentation skills. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the guide on making a presentation. Show signposting phrases.
Feedback on delivery. **Homework:** Prepare a presentation outline.

blocks.heading: Plan 16: Unit 6, The Cyber World
intro: **Book activity:** Speaking: debate on social media. **Focus:** Debating.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to debate the advantages and disadvantages of social media.
**Materials:** Debate topic.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 6: Debating. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Class decides the winning side. **Homework:** Write a paragraph on social media.

blocks.heading: Plan 17: Unit 7, Continuing Education
intro: **Book activity:** Speaking 1; Reading 1. **Focus:** Discussing the future after school.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to discuss feelings about leaving school and read about a technical college.
**Materials:** The discussion questions, Maradana College of Technology text.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 7: Discussing the future after school. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Discuss the questions in pairs and groups. Look at the college picture.
Read the text and answer the questions.
Share one option. **Homework:** Write about your plans after school.

blocks.heading: Plan 18: Unit 7, Continuing Education
intro: **Book activity:** Speaking: table of diplomas; Listening. **Focus:** Asking and answering questions from a table.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to form questions from a table and listen for specific information.
**Materials:** The diploma table, the listening text.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 7: Asking and answering questions from a table. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Show question forms from the table. Pre-teach listening vocabulary.
Groups make ten questions from the table.
Listen to the conversation among four friends and answer.
Share answers. **Homework:** Research one higher-education course.

blocks.heading: Plan 19: Unit 8, Employment
intro: **Book activity:** Reading: advertisements. **Focus:** Reading job advertisements.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to extract key information from job advertisements.
**Materials:** The advertisements.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 8: Reading job advertisements. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Discuss where job advertisements appear. Pre-teach vocabulary.
Read the advertisements and answer the questions.
Choose a job and explain why it suits you.
Share choices. **Homework:** Collect a real job advertisement.

blocks.heading: Plan 20: Unit 8, Employment
intro: **Book activity:** Writing: cover letter. **Focus:** Writing a covering letter.
**Learning outcome:** by the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a covering letter for a job advertisement.
**Materials:** The model letters.
blocks.caption: Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English), Unit 8: Writing a covering letter. A 40-minute PPP lesson.
rows: Read the model letters. Show the structure of a covering letter.
Write a covering letter for one advertisement.

blocks.title: These are samples, not official instructions
text: Each tool is set out in the usual **School Based Assessment tool** format. Fill in your school's name and the date. **For Grades 6 to 11 English, the competency and competency level numbers are taken from the NIE English Language Teachers' Guides** for those grades (see [Competency Levels by Grade](teacher-resources/competency-levels/)). The Grade 6 guide used is the edition implemented from 2015, so schools on the new 2026 Grade 6 syllabus should use the numbers in the new guide. For primary grades, A/L General English and Literature we do not yet have the Teachers' Guides, so the competency wording there is a sample: copy the official competency and level from your guide. Follow the SBA plan and circulars for your grade and year for the number of tools, their timing and how marks are recorded. The terms shown in the Literature tools are suggestions; change them to suit your school's plan.

blocks.title: How to use these
text: Replace the general wording with your school's details. Dates, venues and costs are left for you to fill in, because they depend on your school; check prices locally before you submit a budget. These proposals were written by RCF English and may be copied and adapted freely.

blocks.heading: 1. English Only Day
rows: The Principal, through the relevant sectional head
Many pupils understand English but rarely use it outside the English period. One day a week or a month when English is spoken throughout the school gives them a real reason to use it.
To give pupils regular practice in everyday spoken English; to build confidence; to involve all staff in supporting English.
All pupils from the selected grades, with teachers and non-academic staff.
To be decided with the school administration and entered in the school calendar.
To be decided (for example, the school hall or classrooms).
A short English assembly; English announcements; a list of useful phrases displayed in each classroom; English greetings at the gate; a small reward for classes that use English well.
Teacher in charge; English teachers to prepare phrase lists; prefects to encourage English use; class teachers to record participation.
Phrase charts, a notice board, simple certificates or badges.
List each item with quantity and a local price you have checked. Leave out anything the school already has.
For example, school development funds, class funds or sponsorship. Confirm with the principal.
Class participation records; a short pupil questionnaire after each month.
Pupils use more spoken English and feel less afraid of making mistakes.
Signatures and dates: teacher in charge, sectional head, principal.

blocks.heading: 2. English Day
rows: The Principal, through the relevant sectional head
An annual English Day lets pupils show their English skills to parents and the school community.
To give pupils a stage for English; to discover talent; to raise interest in English.
Pupils of all grades, parents and staff.
To be decided with the school administration and entered in the school calendar.
To be decided (for example, the school hall or classrooms).
Inter-house or inter-class competitions (recitation, speech, singing, drama, spelling); a final programme with the winners; an exhibition of pupils' written work.
Organising committee; competition judges; stage and sound; hospitality; publicity.
Hall, sound system, certificates, trophies or prizes, decorations.
List each item with quantity and a local price you have checked. Leave out anything the school already has.
For example, school development funds, class funds or sponsorship. Confirm with the principal.
Participation numbers, feedback from parents and staff, a short report with photographs.
Greater interest in English and a list of talented pupils for zonal competitions.
Signatures and dates: teacher in charge, sectional head, principal.

blocks.heading: 3. Class Reading Programme
rows: The Principal, through the relevant sectional head
Many pupils read very little in English. A short daily or weekly reading time with a class reading corner builds the reading habit.
To build the reading habit; to improve vocabulary and comprehension.
To be decided with the school administration and entered in the school calendar.
To be decided (for example, the school hall or classrooms).
A class reading corner with graded books; a regular reading time; a simple reading log; a monthly best-reader recognition.
Teacher in charge; class teachers; librarian; pupil reading monitors.
Graded readers, a shelf or box, reading logs.
List each item with quantity and a local price you have checked. Leave out anything the school already has.
For example, school development funds, class funds or sponsorship. Confirm with the principal.
Reading logs; a short reading test at the start and end of the term.
Pupils read more and show better comprehension.
Signatures and dates: teacher in charge, sectional head, principal.

blocks.heading: 4. English Wall Newspaper
rows: The Principal, through the relevant sectional head
A wall newspaper gives pupils a real audience for their writing.
To encourage writing; to develop teamwork; to display pupils' work.
To be decided with the school administration and entered in the school calendar.
To be decided (for example, the school hall or classrooms).
Each class or group produces a wall newspaper in turn with news, notices, stories, poems and puzzles.
Teacher in charge; class editors; a design team for each issue.
List each item with quantity and a local price you have checked. Leave out anything the school already has.
For example, school development funds, class funds or sponsorship. Confirm with the principal.
Quality of issues; number of pupils contributing.
More pupils write in English and take pride in their work.
Signatures and dates: teacher in charge, sectional head, principal.

blocks.heading: 5. English Literary Association
rows: The Principal, through the relevant sectional head
An English club gives interested pupils regular opportunities beyond the classroom.
To provide regular English activities; to prepare pupils for competitions; to develop leadership.
To be decided with the school administration and entered in the school calendar.
To be decided (for example, the school hall or classrooms).
Regular meetings with debates, quizzes, drama, film discussions and guest speakers; election of office bearers.
Teacher in charge; president, secretary and treasurer elected by members.
Meeting room, stationery, a membership register.
List each item with quantity and a local price you have checked. Leave out anything the school already has.
For example, school development funds, class funds or sponsorship. Confirm with the principal.
An active group of pupils who lead English activities in the school.
Signatures and dates: teacher in charge, sectional head, principal.

blocks.heading: 6. Spelling Bee and English Quiz
rows: The Principal, through the relevant sectional head
Competitions make vocabulary and general knowledge practice enjoyable.
To improve spelling and vocabulary; to encourage healthy competition.
Pupils of the selected grades, by class or house.
To be decided with the school administration and entered in the school calendar.
To be decided (for example, the school hall or classrooms).
Class-level rounds followed by a school final; word lists given in advance.
Teacher in charge; question setters; judges; timekeepers.
Word lists, question sheets, a timer, certificates.
List each item with quantity and a local price you have checked. Leave out anything the school already has.
For example, school development funds, class funds or sponsorship. Confirm with the principal.
Better spelling and more interest in words.
Signatures and dates: teacher in charge, sectional head, principal.
